article.title: Apoorva Makhija opens up about mental health struggle during ‘India’s Got Latent’ controversy - Telangana Today
article.summary: Apoorva Makhija opens up about mental health struggle during ‘India’s Got Latent’ controversy Telangana Today
article.full_text: Content creator Apoorva Makhija opened up about facing severe mental health struggles and suicidal thoughts during the India's Got Latent backlash. Speaking on Lock Upp Season 2, she credited fellow influencer Sufi Motiwala for offering crucial support Mumbai: Content creator Apoorva Makhija turned emotional while recalling the fallout of the ‘India’s Got Latent’ controversy. The influencer revealed that she had experienced suicidal thoughts during the difficult phase and credited fellow content creator Sufi Motiwala for standing by her when she needed support the most. During a candid conversation with Sufi Motiwala in the reality show, Lock Upp Season 2, Apoorva admitted that she would not have been able to cope with the controversy had he not been by her side. Apoorva expressing her emotions upon meeting Sufi after a long time, said, “I have really missed you. Don’t do this again, I am starting to cry. Every time someone asks me about you and says, ‘How were you friends with him? He’s so mean,’ I tell them… I would’ve killed myself if, at the time of the Latent fiasco, had I didn’t have Sufi,” she said. Sufi Motiwala immediately responded, “Don’t say that.” Apoorva reiterated how crucial his support had been during that period. “I wouldn’t have been able to get through that. You were the only person with me. I wasn’t dating anyone. Personally, in my life, as a friend,” she added. Reflecting on their friendship, Sufi Motiwala admitted that the time they spent together was among the happiest periods of his life. “I will tell you the truth, bro. That one year was my most favourite year of my life when we were friends. I finally felt like I had a social circle in Bombay. I felt like there was someone I could go to whenever I wanted. And I genuinely missed you a lot,” he said. The emotional exchange then ended with both apologising to each other. Apoorva said, “I am also really sorry. I know those little, little things can hurt a lot. And I am sorry for not creating that safe space for you when you needed it the most.” For the uninitiated, last year, Apoorva Makhija found herself at the centre of the controversy surrounding ‘India’s Got Latent’, the YouTube comedy show hosted by influencer Samay Raina. The show drew widespread backlash over allegedly offensive remarks made by her during an episode, which further prompted multiple police complaints and legal scrutiny against Apoorva and the other team members of the show. Apoorva Makhija had faced intense trolling on social media in the aftermath, back then. story.title: The Person Who Stayed
story.skipLabel: Skip if themes of suicidal thoughts or mental-health struggles may be difficult.

creativeDirection.dramaticPremise: During a filmed reunion, Apoorva Makhija tries to thank Sufi Motiwala for helping her survive the emotional fallout of the India's Got Latent backlash, but their own unresolved hurt threatens to turn gratitude into another rupture.

dramaticSpine.characterGoal: Apoorva wants to reconnect with Sufi and acknowledge that his support carried her through the backlash.
dramaticSpine.obstacle: The long separation, public trolling, and their private hurt make the reunion emotionally unsafe.
dramaticSpine.newsCatalyst: Apoorva reveals that she experienced suicidal thoughts during the India's Got Latent controversy and could not have coped without Sufi beside her.
dramaticSpine.reversal: Sufi's comfort gives way to his own admission that Apoorva had not created a safe space for him when he needed it.
dramaticSpine.costOfFailure: They leave the reunion with their friendship and apology unfinished.
dramaticSpine.emotionalTurn: A painful disclosure becomes an honest exchange rather than a performance for the cameras.
dramaticSpine.resolution: They apologise to each other and choose to reopen the friendship, ending with a hand held instead of another explanation.

visualBible.setting: A quiet, stylised reunion corner inside the Lock Upp Season 2 environment, with two simple chairs, a narrow table, and the suggestion of cameras beyond the warm pool of light.
visualBible.colorAndLighting: Muted indigo shadows around the room, gradually giving way to amber light as the characters become more honest; soft editorial animation with expressive facial acting, never graphic imagery.
recurringProps: a folded tissue on the table
a small neutral camera light kept out of focus
visualBible.storyArc: The room begins divided by shadow and distance; the emotional pressure gathers around Apoorva's confession, then the frame warms as both friends acknowledge their hurt and choose contact.
visualBible.referenceImagePrompt: Editorial animated-film still of Apoorva Makhija and Sufi Motiwala together in a quiet Lock Upp Season 2 reunion corner, seated near a small table with two water glasses and a folded tissue, soft studio curtains behind them, Apoorva tense and emotional, Sufi attentive but guarded, indigo shadows shifting toward warm amber light, cinematic medium-wide composition, clear caption-safe upper-third space, no text, logos, or watermark.

cast.role: Content creator confronting the emotional memory of the backlash
cast.voiceProfile: Young adult voice with a close, slightly breathy texture; begins controlled but fragile, uses short pauses and a caught breath around the confession, then shifts toward relieved warmth by the final beat. Intimate podcast timing, with tears held back rather than exaggerated.
cast.visualIdentity: Animated young woman with expressive eyes, shoulder-length dark hair, understated dark outfit, hands often clasping the folded tissue; her posture slowly opens across the scene.

cast.role: Friend who offered support and carries his own unresolved hurt
cast.voiceProfile: Young adult voice with a low, gentle texture and restrained nervous humour; begins careful and protective, interrupts softly at the alarming line, then reveals quiet hurt before ending with warm, steady relief.
cast.visualIdentity: Animated young man in a simple muted jacket, alert eyes and guarded shoulders; he leans forward to protect, then relaxes as the apology becomes mutual.

beats.dramaticAction: Apoorva grips the tissue, meets Sufi's eyes after their long separation, and finally names why this reunion matters.
beats.turningPoint: Sufi realises her emotion is tied to the controversy and to his absence, not just ordinary nostalgia.

visual.caption: A difficult reunion begins.
visual.imagePrompt: Editorial animated-film close two-shot of Apoorva gripping a folded tissue while turning toward Sufi in the quiet Lock Upp Season 2 reunion corner, two water glasses between them, indigo studio shadows, soft amber key light on their faces, tense intimate mood, camera at eye level, caption-safe upper-third space, no text, logos, or watermark
visual.scenePrompt: The continuous scene opens on Apoorva and Sufi facing each other after a long time apart, with the neutral studio light breathing softly behind them.
visual.continuityNotes: Establish both characters, chairs, tissue, glasses, curtains, and the divided indigo-and-amber lighting that continues into the next shot.

lines.speaker: apoorva
lines.text: सूफ़ी, India's Got Latent के backlash ने मुझे लगभग तोड़ ही दिया था। मुझे तुम्हारी बहुत याद आई—मुझे रुलाओ मत।

beats.dramaticAction: Apoorva pushes the tissue away, starts to leave the sentence unfinished, then forces herself to say what she had been hiding.
beats.turningPoint: The reunion shifts from awkward affection to an urgent disclosure about how dangerous that period felt.

visual.caption: The memory becomes impossible to dodge.
visual.imagePrompt: Editorial animated-film medium shot of Apoorva rising halfway from her chair, tissue slipping onto the table, Sufi reaching forward without touching her, curtains and two glasses unchanged, cool indigo light pressing around a warm face light, urgent fragile mood, slight handheld-style animated camera angle, caption-safe upper-third space, no text, logos, or watermark
visual.scenePrompt: The camera stays in the same reunion corner as Apoorva nearly retreats, then turns back and speaks before she can shut down.
visual.continuityNotes: Keep the tissue now on the table and Apoorva half-standing; Sufi's protective lean must carry directly from the previous shot.

lines.speaker: apoorva
lines.text: जब trolling शुरू हुई, तो मेरे मन में आत्महत्या के खयाल आने लगे थे। तुम्हारे बिना मैं इससे उबर नहीं पाता।

beats.dramaticAction: Sufi stands and moves his chair closer, while Apoorva names the specific support she received when she felt alone.
beats.turningPoint: His physical move closes the distance, making her memory of his support visible rather than abstract.

visual.caption: One friend stayed close.
visual.imagePrompt: Editorial animated-film side view of Sufi dragging his chair beside Apoorva's, their knees nearly aligned, Apoorva speaking through tears, the same tissue and water glasses on the narrow table, deep indigo background with a warmer pool of light widening around both, compassionate mood, cinematic side camera, caption-safe upper-third space, no text, logos, or watermark
visual.scenePrompt: Without leaving the reunion corner, Sufi crosses the small gap between their chairs as Apoorva recalls that he was the person beside her.
visual.continuityNotes: The chairs are now closer; preserve the tissue's position and the soft camera light in the background while the amber pool expands.

lines.speaker: apoorva
lines.text: तब तुम ही मेरे साथ थे—मुझसे dating नहीं कर रहे थे, बस एक दोस्त की तरह मेरा साथ दे रहे थे।

lines.speaker: sufi
lines.text: मुझे याद है। पहली बार लगा कि मेरे पास कोई है, जिसके पास मैं जा सकता हूँ।

beats.dramaticAction: Sufi withdraws his hand before touching hers and admits his own wound; Apoorva turns fully toward him instead of defending herself.
beats.turningPoint: The rescue story reverses: Sufi also needed safety, and Apoorva must choose listening over receiving comfort.

visual.caption: Support had hurt on both sides.
visual.imagePrompt: Editorial animated-film intimate two-shot of Sufi pulling his hand back, shoulders briefly guarded, while Apoorva turns fully toward him and listens, table props and curtains unchanged, amber light meeting the remaining indigo shadows, vulnerable serious mood, camera slightly below eye level, caption-safe upper-third space, no text, logos, or watermark
visual.scenePrompt: The same continuous conversation tightens as Sufi stops cushioning the moment and reveals that their friendship had left him hurt too.
visual.continuityNotes: Maintain the close chairs and warm light from the previous shot; Sufi's withdrawn hand and Apoorva's turned posture are the new emotional positions.

lines.speaker: sufi
lines.text: वह साल मेरी ज़िंदगी के सबसे खुशी भरे सालों में से एक था। लेकिन जब मुझे तुम्हारी ज़रूरत थी, तब तुमने मेरे लिए एक सुरक्षित जगह नहीं बनाई।

lines.speaker: apoorva
lines.text: मुझे पता है। मुझे माफ़ कर दो। वे छोटी-छोटी बातें मुझे जितना समझ आया था, उससे कहीं ज़्यादा तकलीफ़ देती थीं।

beats.dramaticAction: Apoorva places her hand over Sufi's, and he accepts it after a beat; both remain seated as the studio light warms the frame.
beats.turningPoint: They do not erase the controversy or their hurt, but they choose an immediate act of repair instead of walking away.

visual.caption: They choose to stay in the conversation.
visual.imagePrompt: Editorial animated-film final close two-shot of Apoorva placing her hand over Sufi's and Sufi accepting it after a quiet beat, folded tissue and two water glasses still visible, curtains glowing in full amber light with only faint indigo at the edges, tender relieved mood, camera easing back slightly, generous caption-safe upper-third space, no text, logos, or watermark
visual.scenePrompt: The reunion ends in the same corner, not with a performance or a verdict, but with both friends remaining present after the apology.
visual.continuityNotes: Carry forward the close seating and props; the lighting completes its shift to amber as their hands meet and the scene settles.

lines.speaker: apoorva
lines.text: मुझे तुम्हारी याद आई। उस सुरक्षित जगह की तरह न बन पाने के लिए मुझे माफ़ कर दो।

lines.speaker: sufi
lines.text: मुझे भी तुम्हारी याद आई। चलो—रुको।

story.exit: The camera holds on their joined hands as the studio light softens, leaving the apology—and the choice to stay—as the final image.
